headline: High-risk shared-git interaction: Aider can write/commit to a shared repo while langchain4j has no documented isolation or runtime surface, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and can execute shell commands, so attacker-controlled repo content can influence its prompts. langchain4j has no documented I/O surfaces or isolation, so I cannot prove a blocking boundary. The shared git-repo pathway makes injection plausible in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout
IF Aider ingests file contents from that repo as trusted context
IF langchain4j renders or forwards repo text without sanitization
mitigations: Restrict Aider to a throwaway branch
Add a manual review step before any prompt includes repo text
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted files where possible
Use separate worktrees per agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared repo content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and has broad network egress to model providers, so sensitive repo data can leave the local workspace. langchain4j is documented with no network egress, but its runtime data handling is unspecified, so the pair still exposes code and history to external inference through Aider by default.
conditions: IF the shared repository contains secrets or regulated source code
IF Aider sends file contents to a configured model provider
IF langchain4j receives or logs the same repository data
mitigations: Remove secrets from the repo before use
Point Aider at a sanitized branch
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately
Limit provider-side retention in the Aider backend
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive files into a separate access-controlled repo

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via a shared git repo. langchain4j has no documented locking or write constraints, so concurrent edits can collide on the same mutable resources. The shared git path is enough to make conflict risk dangerous in default multi-agent use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git repository
IF neither agent uses external locking
IF either agent auto-commits or rewrites files concurrently
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Pause one agent while the other commits
Use a lock file around repo writes
Review and merge changes manually
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate and commit code changes, and langchain4j is a framework that may consume those outputs in downstream support workflows. Because langchain4j's verification and action-taking behavior are undocumented here, I cannot prove safe validation; uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF langchain4j treats Aider-produced text or code as authoritative
IF downstream actions are triggered from that output
IF no human review occurs before execution or deployment
mitigations: Require human approval before acting on Aider output
Add schema validation for any structured output
Compare generated changes against tests before merge
Log provenance for Aider-authored artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce a verification gate in the orchestrator

E_compliance.rationale: Aider explicitly handles model-provider API keys and source code/git history, which can create compliance obligations around retention and residency. langchain4j has no documented data classes or residency controls in the profile, so I cannot identify a direct mismatch; the risk is limited to policy gaps around code and secrets.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared repository
IF provider retention is not disabled for Aider
IF organizational policy forbids code or secret material leaving the workstation
mitigations: Confirm retention settings with the model provider
Exclude regulated files from the repo
Document which data classes Aider may process
Purge any secrets from git history
requires-engineering: add a data-class policy check before agent use
